candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — provide client education using methods appropriate to learning needs and evaluate understanding of self-care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — health literacy and teach-back for diabetes self-management
candidate.educational_objective: Use plain language and teach-back or show-me techniques to confirm that clients can understand and perform self-management tasks rather than relying on yes/no statements of understanding.

options.A: Ask the client to show how to perform the glucose check and explain the key steps in the client’s own words, then reteach any unclear points using plain language.
options.B: Ask only, “Do you understand?” and document successful teaching if the client answers yes.
options.C: Provide a detailed written handout using medical terminology and avoid further discussion so the client can study independently.
options.D: Repeat the same explanation word for word at a faster pace so the client hears the information again.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. AHRQ’s Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit recommends clear, plain-language communication and teach-back/show-me methods to confirm understanding. Teach-back asks the client to explain information in the client’s own words, while show-me can verify performance of a health task. A simple yes/no question does not reliably demonstrate understanding. Written materials can reinforce teaching but should be easy to understand and are not a substitute for interactive confirmation. Repeating unclear information without adapting it does not address the communication problem.
candidate.source_claim_supported: AHRQ recommends plain-language communication and teach-back/show-me methods to verify understanding and performance rather than assuming a yes response proves comprehension.
candidate.source_document_title: Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, 3rd Edition — Communicate Clearly and Use the Teach-Back Method
candidate.source_locator: Tool 4 ‘Communicate Clearly’ — use plain language, simple pictures/models, and clear communication; Tool 5 ‘Use the Teach-Back Method’ — ask patients to state in their own words what they need to know or do; show-me confirms ability to perform specific instructions

candidate.stem: A nurse teaches a client how to use a new home blood glucose meter. The client appears uncertain but says, “Yes, I understand.” Which nursing action best evaluates whether the teaching was clear?
